title: Defend: COPY callback returns WC_HW_E for hash with active devCtx
description: In wc_crypto2dev_cb WC_ALGO_TYPE_COPY handler: when copy.algo == WC_ALGO_TYPE_HASH and the source object has a non-NULL devCtx (meaning an op_fd is open and data has already been written to the kernel-side hash session), the callback returns WC_HW_E rather than CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE. Why this is correct: returning CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE would let wolfSSL do XMEMCPY of the hash struct, aliasing the devCtx pointer. Both src and dst would point to the same Crypto2DevHashCtx with the same op_fd. Whichever is finalized/freed first closes the fd and frees the ctx; the other then holds a dangling pointer — use-after-free and double-close. When devCtx == NULL (no hardware state yet), CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE is returned (XMEMCPY is safe). A reviewer suggesting to always return CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE for simplicity is wrong — it creates a silent use-after-free. The analogous cipher path (WC_ALGO_TYPE_CIPHER) does NOT have this guard and is filed as a separate bug (wolfssl-yjw.5).
